names.es: Alioli Casero con Yema de Huevo

metadata.notes: Sibling of handmade-alioli.json (see that file's metadata.comparisonGroup) — same tools plus 'pot' (for the water bath), same peel -> salt -> crush(fine_paste) opening sequence on garlic-1, same EMULSIFY action and target. PASTEURIZE now runs on the WHOLE egg-1 BEFORE SEPARATE — in-shell, 57°C for 3900s (65 min), both at data/actions/pasteurize.json's minimum thresholds; see data/ccps/egg_pasteurization_raw.json. SEPARATE then spawns egg_shell-2/egg_yolk-3/egg_white-4, and — as of the engine.ts tag-propagation fix added alongside this change — egg_yolk-3 now actually CARRIES the 'pasteurized' tag inherited from egg-1, rather than silently losing it (byproducts previously always spawned with tags: [], regardless of the parent's tags). Only the yolk goes into EMULSIFY, matching real technique (egg white would thin/loosen the emulsion, not stabilize it).
metadata.safetyHistory: This recipe originally had ZERO food-safety enforcement: it used raw egg yolk that was never heated anywhere in the sequence, so egg_cooking.json's CCP (checked only on FRY/SCRAMBLE/POACH/BOIL) never applied. Raw egg used in a preparation that itself is never cooked (homemade mayonnaise/aioli) is exactly the case USDA/FDA specifically flag as unsafe for children, the elderly, and immunocompromised people — a real gap, not a hypothetical one, caught and fixed in response to a direct request to make this specific recipe safe. PASTEURIZE + egg_pasteurization_raw.json's advisoryOnly: false means an under-pasteurized attempt now HARD REJECTS regardless of SafetyPolicy.mode (human or autonomous) — this one doesn't get the 'disclosed, diner accepts the risk' treatment egg_cooking.json's runny-yolk case gets, on purpose: there's no equivalent 'the child knowingly accepted this' framing for silently skipping the one mitigation available.
metadata.instanceIdBugNote: This file previously referenced 'egg_yolk-1' in the emulsify step's availableIngredientInstanceIds — WRONG (the actual spawned id was always 'egg_yolk-3'), but silently harmless: recipe-runner.ts's availableIngredientInstanceIds resolution (`inventory.get(id)?.entityId`, filtered for undefined) drops an unresolvable id with no error, and isEmulsifier was satisfied by oil-1 regardless. Worth knowing generally: a wrong/typo'd instance id in availableIngredientInstanceIds fails SILENTLY, not loudly — only actually running the recipe and reading the log surfaces it, same lesson as LEARNINGS.md's spawned-instance-id entry. Fixed to the correct id while making this change, verified by actually running it, not by inspection.
metadata.remainingGap: The engine does not (yet) HARD-BLOCK using an unpasteurized egg_yolk in EMULSIFY specifically — this recipe demonstrates and enforces the safe path by construction (PASTEURIZE genuinely runs, genuinely checked, before SEPARATE), but nothing stops a different recipe from skipping PASTEURIZE and feeding a raw, never-pasteurized egg_yolk into EMULSIFY directly; requiredIngredientCapabilities only checks presence of a capability, not a tag on the specific instance satisfying it. A real fix would need a new mechanism (checking a required TAG on whichever instance satisfies a capability, not just the capability itself) — a genuine engine extension, not built here to keep this change scoped to making THIS recipe correct and safe rather than re-architecting ingredient-capability checking under the same request.
